newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: NAB sees big local banks as foreign targets.
newsitem.headline: NAB sees big local banks as foreign targets.

text.p: National Australia Bank Ltd managing director Don Argus said on Thursday that uncertainty about the final design of Australia's financial system meant that the country's major banks had become potential targets for foreign competitors.
"An unintended consequence of the current lack of clarity has been to put all of Australia's major banks in a foreign 'takeover frame'," Argus said in a statement.
He was commenting on the recommendations of the Wallis inquiry into the financial system, which was released by the federal government on April 9.
The report recommended mergers among the big four local banks and the two largest insurance firms and also said it did not object to foreign takeovers of local banks.

The government, however, said it would not permit mergers among the big four banks until the business community received better service and rates from the banks but also said it would allow some foreign takeovers if they met national interest provisions. Treasurer Peter Costello said he would make a more detailed response to the Wallis report after the federal budget was handed down last Tuesday.
National Australia, the nation's largest and most profitable bank, had said in its submission to the Wallis inquiry that the big banks should be allowed to merge.
"Without policy clarity, the Australian banking and financial services system will remain 'unsettled'," Argus said.
He also rejected as illogical the government's argument that the big banks should not be permitted to merge until the banking sector provided improved competition to the small-medium business sector.

"The stated reason for the 'four pillars' policy (which prevents big four bank mergers) is the lack of competitiveness in the business lending market. There may be many reasons for deciding against major bank mergers, but this does not seem to be the most logical," Argus said.

National Australia, which has profitable operations in the United Kingdom and the United States as well, was regarded as a definite predator rather than a potential target before the government issued its response to the Wallis inquiry.

A takeover of NAB would cost more than A$27 billion while A$13-A$14 billion would snare the other three big banks -- Westpac Banking Corp, Commonwealth Bank of Australia, and the Australia and New Zealand Banking Group Ltd.
Banking analysts have said Westpac and ANZ were the most likely takeover targets, citing ABN Amro, Lloyds TSB, HongKong Shanghai Bank, and Standard Chartered as possible buyers.
